legacy-mui-button.description:
Design System Button — Figma V3 compliant

**Figma V3 Variants:**
- **Primary**: Midnight Blue filled (#000f47) - For dashboards & standard CTAs
- **Primary Alt (primaryAlt)**: Gold filled (#ffbf00) - For hero banners & marketing CTAs
- **Secondary**: Outline with midnight blue border - Secondary actions
- **Tertiary**: Transparent/ghost - Minimal actions

variant.description:
Visual style aligned to Figma V3 design system:
- **primary**: Midnight Blue filled (#000f47) - For dashboards & standard CTAs
- **primaryAlt**: Gold filled (#ffbf00) - For hero banners & marketing CTAs (Figma: Primary Alt)
- **secondary**: Outline with midnight blue border - Secondary actions
- **tertiary**: Transparent/minimal - Tertiary actions

Legacy aliases (backward compatible):
- **accent** → maps to primaryAlt
- **outline** → maps to secondary
- **ghost** → maps to tertiary

website-herobanner.description:
Hero Banner Component - Full-width hero section with content + image/video split

Design Pattern:
- Full viewport height (100vh) section
- Two-column layout: Content (50%) | Media (50%)
- Supports video background OR static image
- GSAP entrance animations (fade up + stagger)
- Parallax scroll effect

reactDocgen.description:
Hero Banner Component - Full-width hero section with content + image/video split

Design Pattern:
- Full viewport height (100vh) section
- Two-column layout: Content (50%) | Media (50%)
- Supports video background OR static image
- GSAP entrance animations (fade up + stagger)
- Parallax scroll effect
- Responsive: Stacks on mobile
- Dark variant uses Marsh Midnight Blue background (#000f47)

@example
```tsx
<HeroBanner
  eyebrow="Corporate"
  title="Four powerful brand legacies coming together"
  subtitle="Heading 2"
  description="Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet..."
  primaryCta={{ text: "Download Report", onClick: handleDownload }}
  secondaryCta={{ text: "Talk to Our Experts", onClick: handleContact }}
  vimeoId="123456789"
  imageSrc="/hero-image.jpg"
  imageAlt="Aerial city view"
  variant="dark"
  disableAnimations={false}
/>
```

titleEmphasis.description:
Optional second clause, rendered italic immediately after `title` and
participating in the same per-word entrance stagger — matches the
"signature emphasis" pattern of the brand's newer marketing pages
(regular clause, then an italicized second clause).

primaryCta.description: Primary CTA button - Use variant="primaryAlt" (gold) for hero/marketing or variant="primary" (blue) for dashboards

videoSrc.description: Hero video source URL (takes priority over imageSrc)

vimeoId.description: Vimeo video ID (e.g., "123456789") - takes priority over videoSrc

videoPoster.description: Poster image for video (shown before video loads)

imageSrc.description:
Hero image source URL (fallback when no video). Also the fallback shown
if a Vimeo embed fails to load (blocked/restricted/deleted video) — when
using vimeoId, always pass this too, or a failed embed renders nothing.

variant.description: Background variant: dark (midnight blue) or light

layout.description: Layout style: 'split' (side-by-side) or 'background' (media spans entire background)

maxTitleChars.description: Character limit for the title (truncates with ellipsis)

maxDescriptionChars.description: Character limit for the description (truncates with ellipsis)

showCmsHints.description: Display character counts over the text (Useful for CMS preview mode)

play.description:
Gates the entrance timeline. Defaults to `true` (plays immediately on
mount, the original behavior). Pass `false` to hold the whole entrance
(media reveal, M-logo, eyebrow, title, subtitle, description, CTAs)
paused at its hidden starting state, then flip to `true` once ready —
e.g. synced to `IntroLoader`'s `onComplete`, so the entrance doesn't
play out invisibly behind that overlay and finish before it's ever seen.

showMLogoOverlay.description:
Renders the Marsh "M" mark centered over the media column (split layout
only), formed from two GSAP-animated halves sliding in from opposite
sides — the same motion language as the M-forming animations elsewhere
in the app (see `MArrowAnimationTest.tsx` / `heroIntro.ts`), adapted to
the single `/images/M-logo.svg` asset's two path subpaths instead of
two separate SVG files.

titleLineHeight.description: Overrides the title's line-height (defaults to `var(--typo-hero-h1-line-height)`). Use for tighter display headlines without affecting the shared token's other consumers.

children.description: Extra content rendered in the content column, after the description and before CTAs — e.g. a search bar or chip row that doesn't fit the eyebrow/title/subtitle/description/CTA slots.

showPlayButton.description:
Shows the play/pause control for video/vimeo media even in `layout="background"`
(previously `split`-only, since only split had a natural corner for it). Default `false`
— no behavior change for existing `background`-layout callers.

autoPlayVideo.description:
Whether video/vimeo media autoplays on mount. Default `true` (today's behavior,
unchanged for existing callers). Pass `false` for a "click to play" treatment.

mediaControlsSlot.description:
Extra content rendered alongside the play/pause button (only relevant when
that button is shown) — e.g. a duration label, source attribution, or a
"Silent film" badge, without HeroBanner needing to know what those are.

components-buttongroup.name: ButtonGroup
components-buttongroup.description:
# ButtonGroup

Joins related buttons into one visual unit: adjacent buttons share a single
border and the corners between them flatten, so the group reads as one
control rather than several placed side by side.

**Use it for actions that belong to the same decision** — alignment, undo/redo,
a split action with its menu, an input with its affix.

**Don't use it to save space.** Unrelated actions crammed into a group imply a
relationship that isn't there. If the buttons wouldn't share a sentence
("align left, centre, or right"), they shouldn't share a border.

## Accessibility

The container is `role="group"`, which tells assistive tech the buttons belong
together — but a group with no name announces nothing useful. **Give it an
`aria-label`** unless the relationship is already obvious from a visible
heading or the button labels themselves.

## Sizing

There is **no `size` prop on the group** — upstream shadcn has none either, in
the React or the Vue port. A group's height is simply the height of what it
contains, so set `size` on the child `Button`s (`sm` / `md` / `lg`) and the
group follows. See the **Sizes** and **IconSizes** stories.

## Related

- `ToggleGroup` — when the buttons represent *state* (pressed / not pressed),
  not one-off actions. A text-alignment control that shows which alignment is
  currently active is a ToggleGroup; one that just applies an alignment is a
  ButtonGroup.
- `InputGroup` — when the unit is built around an input rather than buttons.

reactDocgen.description:
Groups related buttons into a single visual unit.

`role="group"` is deliberate: it tells assistive tech these controls belong
together. Pair it with `aria-label` whenever the grouping isn't obvious from
the buttons alone — a bare group announces nothing about what it groups.

A group is the one place where a height mismatch is unmissable, because the
controls share edges. Before the shared control scale existed, an Input
(40px) beside a Button (48px) inside a group left a visible step in what is
supposed to read as a single unit — `items-stretch` could not fix it,
because both children set explicit heights that override stretch.

size.description:
Size for every control in the group. Cascades via context, so a Button,
an Input and a Select in the same group are the same height without the
author repeating it on each — and a mismatched group is not expressible
by accident. A child's own `size` prop still wins.

Every data surface has four states, and a dashboard is mostly the states
around the data rather than the data itself.

components-datatable.name: DataTable
components-datatable.description:
# DataTable

No MDS/Figma spec exists for this component — built matching the standard TanStack-Table-based recipe (`@tanstack/react-table`), reusing
this repo's own `Checkbox`/`Pagination`/`Input`/`DropdownMenu` atoms
rather than duplicating them.

This is a separate, more powerful sibling to `table.tsx`'s hand-rolled
`Table` — reach for `Table` for the common case, `DataTable` when you
need column filtering/visibility toggling on top of sorting/selection/
pagination.

reactDocgen.description:
The table.

Pass `columns` and `data` and it builds and owns the instance — the common
case. Pass `table` as well and you own it instead, while every other prop
keeps working: that is the point of the escape hatch. Reading the selection
or the active filters from outside the table previously meant abandoning
the preset entirely and hand-assembling `DataGrid`'s four children.

    const table = useDataGridTable({ columns, data });
    const picked = table.getSelectedRowModel().rows;      // outside
    <DataTable table={table} columns={columns} data={data} enableExport />

`DataGrid` is still the answer when the PARTS need rearranging — a toolbar
below the table, a replaced footer, a piece left out. This covers the far
more common case of wanting the state, not a different layout.

selectionNoun.description: Noun used in the selection banner, e.g. "policy".

selectionNounPlural.description: Its plural. Defaults to `selectionNoun + "s"` — pass it for anything English does not pluralise that way.

onSelectionChange.description:
Reports the selection AND its scope.

Branch on `allFilteredRowsSelected`: when it is true the user asked for
every record matching the filters, and `selectedRowIds` holds only the
loaded page — send the filter state to your bulk endpoint, not the ids.

table.description:
Own the table instance instead of letting this component build one.

Every other prop keeps working — that is the whole point. Reading the
selection or the active filters from OUTSIDE the table used to mean
abandoning the preset and hand-assembling `DataGrid`'s four children,
which is a steep price for wanting the state rather than a different
layout.

    const table = useDataGridTable({ columns, data });
    <DataTable table={table} columns={columns} data={data} enableExport />

Build it with `useDataGridTable` so it carries this system's defaults: a
bare `useTable` would be missing the filter-fn resolution and the pinning
state that make the grid behave correctly.

Reach for `DataGrid` instead when the PARTS need rearranging.

hold `A AND (B OR C)`. The value model behind `filterFields` cannot.

where a pinned leading column doesn't make sense.

Bounds the table's scroll container to this height and makes the
header sticky within it. Without a bounded height, `position: sticky`
on the header has nothing to stick within — the whole page scrolls

Server-side pagination: `data` is assumed to already be just the

— `data.length` alone only describes the current page.

default `Empty` block, which already distinguishes "no data at all"
from "the current search matched nothing" and offers to clear the
search in the latter case.

Enables inline editing for columns marked `meta: { editable: true }`.

holds no copy of the data, so the handler owns persisting the change.

toggle would never render and the panel would be unreachable. Pass

Named `loadError`, not `error`, to keep it clearly separate from form
validation's `error`/`invalid` — see data-state.tsx. Before this prop
existed a failed request rendered as "No data yet", which looks like an
answer rather than a failure.

stories.name: With Row Selection
Select All Results
stories.description:
**"Select all" must never be ambiguous.**

The header checkbox selects the PAGE — it says so, because that is what it
does. Selecting every record matching the current filters is a separate,
explicit act, and the banner states which scope is in force at all times.

This matters most in server mode: the client holds one page, so "all 1,284"
cannot be a set of selected rows — there are no row objects for the other
1,279. It is a flag about the QUERY. A bulk action must branch on
`allFilteredRowsSelected` and send the filter state, not `selectedRowIds`.

Note each checkbox is named after its record ("Select Commercial Auto"),
not its position: position changes under sorting and filtering.

stories.name: Bulk Actions
stories.description:
**Bulk actions (§10).** Selection exists to enable an operation; until this
landed, it enabled reporting that one *could* happen.

The actions live inside the selection banner rather than a bar of their own,
because the first requirement is that the count context is not hidden from
the button that acts on it.

Three things here are easy to leave out and are why this is a component:

- **Scope in the confirmation.** Escalate to "all results" and the dialog
  changes from "Delete 3 selected policies?" to "Delete all N policies
  matching the current filters?". The copy is generated from the live
  selection, so it cannot drift from what the handler receives.
- **Partial success.** "Assign" here fails one record on purpose. Bulk
  operations half-fail routinely, and a success toast after that is a lie.
- **Permissions.** "Delete" is disabled with a reason, rather than absent.

stories.name: Row Actions
stories.description:
**Row actions (§11).** Most of that section is about restraint: do not
overload every row with visible buttons, promote at most one common action,
and move the rest into overflow.

So: one `View` button, everything else behind the menu, destructive items
separated and confirmed.

Each control is named after its record — "More actions for Commercial
Auto", not forty buttons called "More actions". And acting on a row does not
fire `onRowClick`: §34 lists that conflict explicitly, and this column is the
case that breaks it if the markup drifts.

components-filterbar.description:
# FilterBar

The page-level filter row.

Four bespoke filter rows shipped in this repo sharing nothing, and **none
of them showed the user what was currently filtering their view**. A
dashboard that silently hides rows is one people stop trusting — "where
did my policy go?" had no answer on screen. `FilterBarChips` is the part
that fixes that.

**FilterBar vs DataTable's faceted filters** — not alternatives. FilterBar
filters the *dataset* and drives the query; `facetedFilters` filter
*within* the rows already fetched, per column, with counts. Using both for
the same field gives you two controls that disagree.

identically-named regions with no way to tell them apart.

components-filterfieldcontrol.name: FilterFieldControl
components-filterfieldcontrol.description:
One `FilterField` definition in, the right control out.

This is the piece that lets a filter be defined **once**. Before it, the two
filter systems each decided independently which control a field got:
`DataGridToolbar` took `facetedFilters` and `dateFilters` as separate props
keyed by column id, and `FilterBar` took hand-placed children. Adding a field
meant editing both, in different shapes, and neither could tell you what the
complete filter set was.

It is deliberately dumb: it holds **no state** and knows nothing about
tables. The caller owns the value and decides what a change means — a local
`setState`, a column filter, a server query, a URL parameter. That is what
makes one definition usable in all four places.

### Choosing between this and `components/ui/filters`

This is a **value model**: a field and a value, with no operator. It cannot
express "is not", "is any of" or "between", and cannot represent
`A AND (B OR C)` at all. Reach for the query system in
`components/ui/filters` when you need operators or a nested tree — that is
also what lets it serialise to a URL.

components-notificationsdrawer.description:
The risk-notification panel — a `Sheet` listing weather, catastrophe and
policy alerts against insured locations.

Rebuilt from the MUI `NotificationsDrawer` on `Sheet` rather than MUI
`Drawer`. Severity colours go through `getRoleColor()` and so adapt to dark
mode, which the MUI original's static per-severity hex map does not — that

the nearest existing `status.*` role. `watch` is the one to know about: its
foreground is `text.onLight`, **not** `status.warning.fg` — warning gold on
warning background measures 3.34:1, which is fine as an accent and
unreadable as text.

components-pageshell.description:
# PageShell

The dashboard page **template** — slots only, no business data.

It exists because the scaffold is genuinely easy to get wrong. The sidebar
is `fixed` with a scrim below `lg` and `static` above it, and there is a
`min-w-0` chain that must run down *every* flex ancestor between the page
and a wide table. Miss one link in that chain and the whole page scrolls
sideways — a bug that presents as a table bug and isn't.

Pair it with `PageHeading` for the title / description / actions row.

header.description: Rendered above everything, full width. Typically `<Header />`.

sidebar.description:
Rendered beside the main column. Becomes an overlay drawer below `lg`,
where `sidebarOpen` controls it.

sidebarOpen.description: Mobile drawer state. Ignored at `lg` and above, where the sidebar is static.

onSidebarClose.description: Called when the mobile scrim is clicked.

contained.description: Constrain the main column to the 1540px MDS container. Defaults to `true`.

skipLink.description:
Renders a "Skip to main content" link as the first focusable element.
On by default.

A dashboard puts a header and a full side navigation ahead of the
content, so a keyboard user otherwise tabs through every nav item on
every page before reaching anything. This is the fix for the one
accessibility claim on the product page that the codebase could not
substantiate — skip links existed in two marketing pages and nowhere in
the dashboard product itself.

# Stack / Inline

The layout atoms. `Stack` is vertical, `Inline` is horizontal and wraps.

Their job is to make the spacing scale a **type**. `gap` accepts only steps
that exist in `src/spacing.ts`, so `gap={7}` (28px — off-scale) is a

whole reason to prefer them over hand-writing `flex flex-col gap-6`.

For two-dimensional layout, use the grid utilities in **Foundations →
Grid System** instead — a Stack is one-dimensional by design.
